hero.started: Hearings are in session — good luck to all!

body: A courtroom is shaped not only by the laws it upholds, but by the minds that challenge, interpret, and redefine them.

As Director General of Themis Court, I welcome you to an experience that invites you to think boldly, argue thoughtfully, and see beyond your own perspective. May this journey challenge your convictions, broaden your horizons, and leave you with more questions worth pursuing.
Themis Court is not simply a place to present arguments, but a place to discover the value of your voice.
Welcome to Themis Court. The floor is yours.

secretary.greeting: Dear esteemed participants of Themis Court Simulations’27,
body: It is a great honor for me to welcome you to the 11th year of Themis Court Simulations as the Secretary General of this conference.

In the 11th year of our conference, we are combining the experience and success built over the years with our own ideas and energy. We are working hard with our brilliant young and academic team to provide you with an unforgettable experience.

This year, we have prepared six different courts for you, and I am very excited to announce them: Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Anayasa Mahkemesi (AYM), Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi (ACM), the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), the Istanbul Arbitration Centre (ISTAC), the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO).

For us, Themis Courts is more than just a simulation. It is an opportunity to learn from one another, challenge our perspectives, and create meaningful connections along the way. I am truly honored to be part of this journey and to work alongside such a dedicated team. We look forward to welcoming you all and creating an unforgettable experience together.
Wishing you a pleasant moot court experience.

courts.title: Courts
courts.subtitle: Choose from six courts — four in Turkish and two in English.

cas.name: Court of Arbitration for Sport
cas.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) is an independent dispute resolution body that settles sports-related disputes through arbitration. In addition to disputes of an international nature, it hears appeals against decisions rendered at the national level, within the framework of the regulations and jurisdictional rules of the relevant sports federations. Doping violations, disciplinary sanctions imposed on athletes, and disputes between athletes, clubs and sports organisations are the main types of cases heard by the court.

istac.name: Istanbul Arbitration Centre
istac.description: The Istanbul Arbitration Centre (ISTAC) is an independent, impartial and autonomous institution that enables domestic and international commercial disputes to be resolved through arbitration and mediation. In line with the parties’ agreement, it examines disputes arising from contracts and ensures that binding awards are rendered through arbitration.

acm.name: High Criminal Court
acm.description: The High Criminal Court is a first-instance court in the Turkish legal system that hears criminal cases concerning serious offences defined by law. It hears cases involving certain offences listed in the law other than robbery, extortion by public officials and aggravated fraud, terrorism offences, and offences punishable by aggravated life imprisonment, life imprisonment or imprisonment of more than ten years.

aym.name: Constitutional Court of Türkiye
aym.description: The Constitutional Court is the highest constitutional judicial body in Türkiye, safeguarding the supremacy of the Constitution. It reviews the constitutionality of laws and presidential decrees. It also examines applications from individuals who believe their fundamental rights and freedoms have been violated. It carries out the financial audit of political parties and, in cases specified by law, hears cases for the dissolution of political parties.

echr.name: European Court of Human Rights
echr.topic: Violations of the European Convention on Human Rights
echr.description: The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) is an international court responsible for protecting the fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed by the European Convention on Human Rights. It examines applications brought by individuals, groups, and states alleging violations of the Convention by member states of the Council of Europe. It delivers binding judgments determining whether a state has violated the Convention and may award compensation to victims.

wipo.name: World Intellectual Property Organization
wipo.description: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for promoting the protection of intellectual property worldwide. It develops international intellectual property standards, administers systems for the international registration and protection of patents, trademarks, and industrial designs, and provides mechanisms for resolving intellectual property disputes. It also supports international cooperation and innovation in the field of intellectual property.

venue.title: Kadir Has University Cibali Campus
venue.description: The conference takes place at Kadir Has University's Cibali Campus, housed in the historic Cibali Tobacco Factory on the shore of the Golden Horn — in the heart of the historic peninsula and easy to reach by public transport.
venue.address: Kadir Has University Cibali Campus, Cibali Mah. Kadir Has Cad., 34083 Fatih / Istanbul
highlights: The restored historic Cibali Tobacco Factory building
Session and event spaces overlooking the Golden Horn
The T5 tram's Cibali stop is right opposite the main entrance; about a 10-minute walk from the M2 Haliç station

logistics.title: How Do I Reach the Campus?
logistics.subtitle: Wherever you arrive from, here is a step-by-step guide to the campus.

airport.title: From the Airport
steps: At Istanbul Airport, take the M11 Gayrettepe–Istanbul Airport metro.
Transfer to the M2 line at Gayrettepe, heading towards Yenikapı.
Get off at Haliç (Golden Horn) station.
Walk from Haliç station to the campus (~10 min).

metro.title: Within the City
steps: Tram: take the T5 Eminönü–Alibeyköy line to the Cibali stop, right opposite the campus's main entrance.
Metro: take the M2 Yenikapı–Hacıosman line to Haliç station and walk to the campus (~10 min).
Bus: lines such as 99, 99A, 36CE, 48E or 399C stop at "Unkapanı-Kadir Has Üniversitesi".
Ferry: from Eminönü pier, the same bus lines take you to the Unkapanı-Kadir Has Üniversitesi stop.

bus.title: From the Bus Terminal
steps: From the Grand Istanbul (Esenler) Bus Terminal, take the M1A metro to Yenikapı.
Transfer to the M2 line at Yenikapı and get off at Haliç station.
Walk from Haliç station to the campus (~10 min).
If you arrive at Alibeyköy Coach Station, the T5 tram takes you directly to the Cibali stop.
